newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: INTERVIEW - S.Lanka DFCC sees profits up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - S.Lanka DFCC sees profits up.

text.p: Sri Lanka's DFCC Bank said on Wednesday it would strive for a net profit this financial year above the 590 million rupees ($10.03 million) reported for 1995/96 (April-March).
Company executives told Reuters in an interview that full year 1997/98 net profits should be better than those for 1996/97.

DFCC deputy general manager for finance Subramaniam Nagarajah told Reuters in an interview the institution had faced a difficult year in 1996/97 when its net profit dipped to 471 million rupees from 590 million the year before.
But he said the signs so far this year were much better.
Asked if DFCC could match the 1995/96 total net profit of 590 million rupees, Nagarajah replied:
"I would say we will strive to better it."
DFCC chief executive Moksevi Prelis told Reuters the first three months of the group's 1997/98 financial year suggested many things in the Sri Lankan economy had turned around.
On Tuesday, DFCC reported a net profit of 119 million rupees for its first quarter to June 30, up 29 percent year-on-year.
The improvement was achieved on a quarterly income of 643 million rupees, against 554 million the year before.
Prelis said increased economic activity was leading to higher lending to industry and a higher net profit.
"This year we can definitely see an upturn," he said. "This year will certainly be better than last year. We can already see the signs."
DFCC earlier announced it had changed its name to reflect its new status as a specialist bank.
